title: Dubai or Tenerife in winter: which is better?
author: Matt
intro: Dubai and Tenerife are two of the UK's favourite winter sun trips, but they're very different holidays. Dubai is a few degrees warmer, with big hotels, beaches and city sights, but it's a seven-hour flight and four hours ahead. Tenerife is closer, on UK time and usually cheaper. Here's how to choose.
seo_title: Dubai or Tenerife in winter? Weather, cost and flights
seo_description: Dubai is about 24-26°C in winter but 7 hours away; Tenerife is about 22°C, 4½ hours away and on UK time. Weather, cost, sea and flights compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warmer:** Dubai, by 2 to 4°C
- **Shorter flight:** Tenerife, 4½ hrs
- **No jet lag:** Tenerife, on UK time
- **Usually cheaper:** Tenerife

Pick Dubai for guaranteed warmth, a warm sea and a city break with your beach week. Pick Tenerife for an easy, better-value trip with a shorter flight, especially for a week or less or with young children.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.text:
| | [Dubai](/destinations/dubai) | [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| December high | about 26°C | about 22°C |
| January high | about 24°C | about 22°C |
| February high | about 25°C | about 22°C |
| Sea in January | about 22-23°C | about 19°C |
| Flight from London | about 7 hrs | about 4¼ to 4½ hrs |
| Time difference | +4 hrs in winter | none |

The air temperatures are average daytime highs from our guides. Both are sunny most days in winter. Dubai's evenings are pleasant but can feel cool, while Tenerife's are mild in the south, so you'll want a light jacket in either.

sections.heading: Weather and the sea
sections.text:
Dubai is the warmer of the two all winter, and the difference shows most in the sea. In January the Gulf is around 22 to 23°C, comfortable for swimming, while the Atlantic off Tenerife is about 19°C, which many people find bracing.

Tenerife's south coast, around Costa Adeje and Los Cristianos, is sunny and dry in winter but can have cloudy or breezy days. Dubai rarely has a grey day in winter, though the occasional rain shower does happen.

Tip: if a warm sea matters most, Dubai is the clear winner. If you mostly swim in the hotel pool, the difference is much smaller, as many Tenerife hotels heat their pools in winter.

sections.heading: Cost and getting there
sections.text:
- **Flights:** Tenerife has direct flights from almost every UK airport, often at low fares outside school holidays. Dubai has direct flights from several UK airports with Emirates and others, but it's a longer, usually dearer flight.
- **Hotels and eating out:** Tenerife is usually cheaper day to day. Dubai has hotels at every level, but meals, drinks and attractions add up quickly.
- **Time:** Dubai's seven-hour flight and four-hour time difference make it better for at least a week. Tenerife works for a long weekend.

Dubai's winter peak is busy and expensive, especially around Christmas and New Year. Tenerife's busiest weeks are Christmas, New Year and February half term.

sections.heading: Things to do
sections.text:
- **In Dubai:** the view from the Burj Khalifa, the old souks and an abra ride across Dubai Creek, a desert safari, big water parks and some of the world's largest malls. The Dubai Shopping Festival runs from 4 December 2026 to 17 January 2027, with sales, fireworks and concerts.
- **In Tenerife:** the cable car up Mount Teide, Spain's highest mountain, whale and dolphin trips, the Siam Park water park and Loro Parque, and walks in the Masca gorge and Teno mountains.

Dubai has more of a city break built in, while Tenerife is better for nature and the outdoors. Both suit families, with big water parks and plenty of all-inclusive hotels.

sections.heading: Rules and things to know
sections.text:
Dubai has stricter laws than most UK holiday spots, including on medicines, public behaviour and alcohol, which is mainly served in hotels and licensed venues. UK visitors don't need a visa in advance. Ramadan in 2027 is expected to start in early February, which brings shorter daytime opening hours and rules on eating and drinking in public, so check the dates if you're going in February.

Tenerife is part of Spain and the EU, so it's familiar and relaxed for UK visitors. Check GOV.UK for the latest entry rules for both before you book.

Watch out: some common UK medicines, including some strong painkillers, are controlled in the UAE. Check GOV.UK's advice before you pack.

sections.heading: Which should you choose?
sections.text:
- **Choose Dubai** for guaranteed warmth, a warm sea and a mix of beach and city, for a week or longer.
- **Choose Tenerife** for a shorter, cheaper trip with no jet lag, mountains and outdoor days.
- **For young children:** Tenerife's shorter flight and lack of time difference usually win.

For more ideas, see [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january), our [winter sun with no jet lag](/blog/winter-sun-with-no-jet-lag) post, or [Tenerife or Lanzarote in winter](/blog/tenerife-or-lanzarote-in-winter) if you're set on the Canaries. Still can't agree? Add both to somewhere.party, vote with points and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Is Dubai or Tenerife warmer in winter?
faqs.answer: Dubai is warmer, at about 24 to 26°C by day from December to February, compared with about 22°C in Tenerife. The sea in Dubai is also warmer, at around 22 to 23°C in January.

faqs.question: Is Dubai or Tenerife cheaper?
faqs.answer: Tenerife is usually cheaper, with shorter, lower-cost flights and cheaper meals and drinks. Dubai can be good value in some hotels, but it adds up quickly.

faqs.question: How long is the flight to Dubai and Tenerife?
faqs.answer: About seven hours to Dubai and four and a quarter to four and a half hours to Tenerife from London.

faqs.question: Is Dubai good for a winter holiday with children?
faqs.answer: Yes, with big water parks, beaches and warm weather, but the seven-hour flight and four-hour time difference are harder with young children. Tenerife is easier for a short trip.
